text: Sign in to accounts without a password using a fingerprint, face recognition, or PIN
quote: Microsoft Authenticator is a free app that helps you sign in to all your accounts without using a password - just use a fingerprint, face recognition, or a PIN.

text: Passwordless mode where approving a prompt on the phone is the only way to sign in
quote: As the only way to sign in - just tap an approval on your phone to sign in. This is called going passwordless.

text: Verification codes work without internet, data, or phone service
quote: The codes don't require you to be on the internet or connected to data, so you don't need phone service to sign in.

text: Receive MFA push requests on the phone and approve or deny sign-in attempts
quote: Users can receive an MFA request on their mobile device, and approve or deny the sign-in attempt from their phone.

text: Number matching: enter the number shown at sign-in before approving the request
quote: Tap or enter the corresponding number, then Approve.

text: Location sharing checks hourly that the user is still in a country allowed to access the resource
quote: You'll need to share your location once every hour to ensure you're still within a country where you are allowed to access the resource.

text: One-time password codes for two-step verification or multi-factor authentication
quote: As a way to sign in every time, by using a one-time password code to increase account security. This is called two-step verification or multi-factor authentication.

text: Enter an OATH verification code from the app into a sign-in interface
quote: They can also use an OATH verification code in the Authenticator app and enter it in a sign-in interface.

text: Works with many accounts, including Microsoft, work/school, and third-party accounts like Google and Amazon
quote: You can use Microsoft Authenticator for multiple accounts, including Microsoft personal accounts; work/school accounts; and non-Microsoft accounts, such as Amazon, Facebook, Instagram and Google.

text: Sign in with passkeys stored in the app, giving phishing-resistant authentication through biometrics or device PIN
quote: Users can sign in with a passkey in the Authenticator app and complete phishing-resistant authentication with their biometric sign-in or device PIN.

text: Passkeys are device-bound and never leave the device they were created on
quote: Passkeys in the Authenticator app are device-bound to ensure that they never leave the device they were created on.

text: Passkey support built on open WebAuthn standards
quote: Users stay up-to-date with latest passkey innovation based upon open WebAuthn standards.

text: Store Verified ID credentials that websites and organizations can use to simplify account setup
quote: Verified IDs are secure trusted credentials that can be used by websites and organizations to make account setup simpler and safer.

text: Get a new Verified ID or verify an existing one by scanning a QR code on a site
quote: Usually, you'll use your device's camera to capture a QR code on the site to get a new Verified ID, or a verification of an ID already on your device.

text: Usage history on each Verified ID card shows which sites requested it
quote: Sites that request your Verified ID will show up in the usage history in the details of your Verified ID card.

text: Mirror Authenticator notifications from the phone to a wearable device
quote: you can mirror Authenticator notifications from your phone to your wearable device.

text: App Lock requires the device PIN or a biometric each time the app opens
quote: When App Lock is enabled, you'll be asked to authenticate using your device PIN or biometric every time you open Authenticator.

text: Screen capture of OTP codes is blocked by default and can be turned on in Settings
quote: To see your OTP codes in screenshots or allow other apps to capture the Authenticator screen, turn on Screen Capture in Authenticator's Settings and restart the app.

text: Back up accounts and restore them on a new or replacement device
quote: This article describes how to back up information on all the accounts you have in Authenticator so that if you lose your mobile or get a new device, you can sign in to restore previously saved accounts

text: Cloud backup of OTP codes for Microsoft personal and third-party accounts, stored in a Microsoft personal account
quote: Microsoft Authenticator backs up one-time password codes for eligible Microsoft personal accounts and third-party accounts, such as LinkedIn and Facebook.

text: On iOS, back up OTP codes and account names through iCloud Drive, iCloud Keychain, and iCloud Backup
quote: To back up your Authenticator one-time password codes and account names on an iOS device, enable iCloud Drive, iCloud Keychain, and iCloud Backup for Authenticator.

text: Delete an existing backup or remove one created under the wrong account
quote: If you want to delete a backup, or if you signed in with the wrong backup account, follow these steps:

text: Export saved Autofill passwords for import into another password provider
quote: Scroll down to the Autofill section and select Export Passwords... Import your passwords.

text: Choose whether to share extra non-personal usage data with a Usage Data toggle
quote: You can also allow the sharing of additional non-personal usage data by turning on the "Usage Data" toggle button on the app's Settings page.

text: Diagnostic logs stay on the device until the user sends feedback to Microsoft
quote: Diagnostic log data that stays only in the app until you select Send feedback in the app's top menu to send logs to Microsoft.

text: Add an account by typing the code manually when the QR code can't be scanned
quote: If you can't use your camera to scan a QR Code, click **I can't scan the bar code** on your PC and tap **Enter code manually** on your mobile.

text: Sign in on a remote screen by entering the code shown in Authenticator
quote: On the remote screen, open the Sign in to your account page and enter the code that you see in Authenticator.

text: Sign in with a Temporary Access Pass during setup
quote: If you have a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) you can use that to sign in.

text: Use the app as a verification method for self-service password reset and MFA
quote: They can also use it as a verification option during self-service password reset (SSPR) or multifactor authentication (MFA) events.
